active.body:
`loom` has reported the same newest epoch, MJD 61359.23043, on every run since 2026-11-17T00:27:16Z — 10.9 days, against a limit of 7. Source: `results/loom/screen.json` → `frontier_mjd`.

Observed cadence so far: 3 advance(s), median 7.033 d, longest gap 95.434 d.

The channel is running and committing normally; what has stopped is the mirror. Every null it reports while this holds means *no new sky*, not *clean sky*, and the two are not the same result.

Check whether ALeRCE is still ingesting the LSST alert stream. If the pause turns out to be ordinary batching, raise `FRONTIER_STALL_DAYS` using the cadence recorded in `results/alerts/frontier.json` rather than by guessing again.

**Cause established 2026-11-24 by `rubin-outage`: SKY_STOPPED.** Independent brokers stop on the same night (ALeRCE 2026-11-15; fink 2026-11-15), so the alert stream itself stopped and no change to the broker path recovers data that was never taken. Do not relax the threshold on this — the condition is real. See `docs/rubin-outage.md`. ZTF, the other public wide-field alert stream, is LIVE (newest night 2026-11-23 via archive), so `tocsin-altfeeds` has a current feed to lean on.
active.title: LOOM's data frontier has not advanced in 11 days

active.body:
`tocsin` has advanced from MJD 61359.23189 to MJD 61371.26872 — 12.0 days of sky — after sitting still since 2026-11-15T19:49:44Z.

The stall was confirmed across 11.2 days of sightings; the advance itself happened between 2026-11-27T00:59:50Z and now, so the interval between successive frontier values is 12.1 days. That is an UPPER BOUND on the mirror's true ingest gap — this repository samples the frontier about once a day and cannot see a change finer than that.

The frontier is now 0.7 days behind the wall clock, inside the 30-day limit, so the age alert clears. That is not the same as current: the mirror's ordinary lag is ~16 days, and anything above that is still backlog.

This is the cadence datum `FRONTIER_STALL_DAYS` has never had — it was set to 7 by guesswork because no advance had ever been observed here. Recalibrate it against `observed_advance_days` in `results/alerts/frontier.json` now that there is one.

Note that the nights lost to the stall are ABSENT, not null: they were never observed, so they add nothing to the screen's trial count and must not be counted as clean sky.
active.title: TOCSIN's data frontier is moving again (+12.0 days of sky)

active.body:
The `asassn` adapter reached its service but has no usable path to a light curve.

Reason recorded by the probe: no cone request was accepted (every variant and format in the matrix above), and the vendor client cannot be imported here -- so there is no path to a light curve, only to metadata

A screen over this feed would run, commit and report nothing found -- which is indistinguishable from a quiet sky and is not a result. Read `results/tocsin_altfeeds/probe.json`; the request matrix there records responses and connection errors.
active.title: ASASSN cannot serve light curves
